legend: You are given an array a$$$a$$$ of n$$$n$$$ distinct positive integers. Unfortunately, the array is way past its prime, so you have decided to help it relive "the good old days"!

The array remembers that in the "the good old days" it had a sum of elements greater than or equal to a given threshold s$$$s$$$. To help the array, you are allowed to perform a sequence of operations. In one operation, you may choose any positive integer x$$$x$$$ which is not already present in the array, and append it to the end of a$$$a$$$.

In a stroke of genius and insecurity, you have come to the rational conclusion that once the array realizes that the sum of its elements is greater than or equal to s$$$s$$$, it will no longer allow you to perform any more operations and leave forever. To postpone the inevitable departure of the array, you have decided to make the helping process as lengthy as possible. More formally, you would like to maximize the number of operations before the array realizes that the sum of its elements is greater than or equal to s$$$s$$$.
What is the maximum final length of array a$$$a$$$?
input: The first line of input contains two integers n$$$n$$$ and s$$$s$$$ (1≤n≤2⋅105$$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$, 1≤s≤1018)$$$1 \le s \le 10^{18})$$$ — the length of the initial array, and the given threshold for the sum. The second line of input contains n$$$n$$$ integers a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$$$ (1≤ai≤1012$$$1 \le a_i \le 10^{12}$$$) — the elements of the initial array.
output: Print one integer, the maximum possible final length of the array.
note: In the first sample, a way to get an array of size 6$$$6$$$ is to append, in order, integers 4$$$4$$$, 2$$$2$$$ and 7$$$7$$$, giving us the array a=[6,1,3,4,2,7]$$$a=[6,1,3,4,2,7]$$$. When 7$$$7$$$ is appended, the sum of the elements will become 6+1+3+4+2+7=23$$$6+1+3+4+2+7=23$$$, which is greater than or equal to s=17$$$s=17$$$.
In the second sample, the sum of the elements of the array is 6+8+1+5+9=29$$$6+8+1+5+9=29$$$, which is already greater than or equal to s=28$$$s=28$$$.

legend.ai: 给定一个包含 n$$$n$$$ 个互不相同的正整数的数组 a$$$a$$$。遗憾的是，这个数组早已过了巅峰时期，因此你决定帮助它重温“美好的旧时光”！
这个数组记得，在“美好的旧时光”中，它的元素总和大于或等于给定的阈值 s$$$s$$$。为了帮助这个数组，你可以执行一系列操作。每次操作中，你可以选择任意一个数组中尚未出现的正整数 x$$$x$$$，并将其追加到 a$$$a$$$ 的末尾。
经过一番天才般又略带不安的思考，你得出了一个合理的结论：一旦数组意识到其元素总和大于或等于 s$$$s$$$，它就不会再允许你执行任何操作，并将永远离开。为了推迟数组不可避免的离去，你决定让帮助过程尽可能长。更正式地说，你希望最大化数组意识到其元素总和大于或等于 s$$$s$$$ 之前所执行的操作次数。
数组 a$$$a$$$ 最终可能的最大长度是多少？

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含两个整数 n$$$n$$$ 和 s$$$s$$$(1≤n≤2⋅105$$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$，1≤s≤1018)$$$1 \le s \le 10^{18})$$$ —— 分别表示初始数组的长度，以及给定的总和阈值。输入的第二行包含 n$$$n$$$ 个整数 a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$$$(1≤ai≤1012$$$1 \le a_i \le 10^{12}$$$)—— 表示初始数组的元素。

output.ai: 输出一个整数，表示数组最终可能的最大长度。
